mechanism: CME Bitcoin/Ether futures cash-settle on the last Friday of each month. In the post-spot-ETF regime (since Jan 2024), authorized participants and CTAs that run the futures-basis/roll trade must source or unwind large spot/futures positions timed to that monthly settlement, and ETF creation-basket flows cluster around the same roll window. A published expiration-effects study finds statistically significant abnormal returns in the three days before CME BTC expiry that reversed sign after the BITO ETF launched in Oct 2021 -- i.e. the settlement date is a forced-flow event, not noise, and its sign is regime-dependent on ETF-driven flow. The forced counterparty is the basis-trade/roll desk (CTAs, ETF APs) that must transact spot/futures around a fixed calendar date regardless of discretionary view.
counterparty: CME BTC/ETH futures basis-trade unwind/roll flow and ETF authorized-participant creation-basket sourcing, both mechanically timed to the last-Friday-of-month CME cash settlement -- forced transacting that this thesis rides for 3 days into settlement.
prediction: In the post-ETF regime, BTC and ETH show a directional drift in the 72h before CME's last-Friday-of-month settlement (15:00 UTC proxy for 4pm London) that is measurable net of the 11.5bps round-trip cost and clears p*(200bps)=52.875% (fee_math.p_star, cited in mandate.md section 3); this spec is registered long-only for that window per the paper's reported post-BITO reversal of the pre-ETF negative pre-expiry drift, to be confirmed or refuted by the screen -- not asserted as already measured by us.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 7 killed 'CME gap fill' specifically as a chart-gap artifact from CME's closed trading hours vs. continuous crypto markets -- a microstructure/liquidity effect with no forced counterparty. This thesis is about the CME cash-settlement date itself forcing basis-trade unwind and ETF creation-basket flow, a completely different mechanism (settlement-driven capital flow, not a trading-hours price gap).

Row 33 (BTC/ETH Donchian-ensemble trend) is a trend-following indicator strategy the owner declined to ever re-offer live. This thesis is calendar-gated to a specific externally documented 72h pre-settlement window, not an always-on trend signal, and the entry/exit is keyed to a fixed CME date, not a Donchian breakout.

Row 84 (FOMC/CPI first-candle momentum) needed 1-minute precision the bot cannot deliver and is intraday. This thesis holds 3-4 days into a monthly settlement using 1h bars, well within the bot's 5-minute poller resolution, and the forced flow (futures roll/basis unwind) is a multi-day institutional positioning process, not a single macro-print candle reaction.

evidence: QuantPedia summary of a Bitcoin-futures-expiration-effects study (sample Dec 29 2017 - Feb 28 2024, CME BTC futures expiring last Friday of month at 4pm London time): pre-BITO (through Sep 24 2021), returns were negative on days t-3 to t-1 before expiry and expiry day itself showed positive returns; this pattern reversed after the Oct 2021 BITO ETF launch, and the authors report 'significant changes in the trading volume, volatility, and returns of bitcoin' around maturity across the full 2017-2024 sample. The PMC paper 'The witching week of herding on bitcoin exchanges' independently corroborates that herding/expiry effects are concentrated in the week before CME expiration and dissipate within hours afterward. I was not able to extract the exact post-BITO effect-size percentage from either fetched summary (only direction of the pre-BITO/post-BITO reversal was reported to me) -- that gap is disclosed in the prediction field rather than invented.
